## **Left Sidebar (Navigation)** {#left-sidebar-(navigation)}

**What it does:** The sidebar is the main menu of the app. It sits on the left side of the screen and stays visible at all times, so users can jump between sections without getting lost or needing to go "back."

**What's in it:**

* **Navigation links** — the main sections/pages of the app (e.g., Home, Recruitment, Employees, Time & Leave, Payroll, Reimbursement, Attendance, Reports)  
* **Logged-in user info at the bottom** — shows who is currently logged in. This usually includes:  
  * The user's name and/or photo/avatar  
  * Their role or account type (if relevant)  
  * Access to their **profile** (clicking it lets them view/edit their account details, or log out)

## **Top Bar (Navigation)** {#top-bar-(navigation)}

**What it does:** The top bar sits above the main content area and stays visible on every page. It contains two key tools: a **search bar** and a **notification bell**.

### **Search Bar** {#search-bar}

* Lets users search across the app instead of manually clicking through menus.  
* Should return relevant results quickly (e.g., a request, a record, a person, a document — whatever is searchable in the app).  
* Saves time for users who know what they're looking for but don't want to navigate multiple pages to find it.

### **Notification Bell** {#notification-bell}

* Shows a **bell icon** with a **number badge** on it.  
* The number represents **how many items need the user's attention** right now (e.g., pending approvals, unread updates, action-required items).  
* Clicking the bell opens a list of those notifications/items.  
* Once the user views or resolves an item, the count goes down.

## **Toasts (Pop-Up Confirmations)** {#toasts-(pop-up-confirmations)}

**What they are:** Toasts are small, temporary pop-up messages that appear briefly on the screen (usually in a corner) whenever something happens in the app. They disappear on their own after a few seconds.

**When they appear (examples):**

* A request is submitted → *"Your request has been submitted."*  
* A request is approved → *"Request approved."*  
* A payment goes through → *"Payment successful."*

## **Dashboard — The HR Home Screen** {#dashboard-—-the-hr-home-screen}

The Dashboard is the **first screen HR sees** when they open the app. It's meant to answer the question *"What's going on right now?"* in one glance — without having to click into other pages. It has four parts: **stat cards**, a **headcount & attrition chart**, a **pending approvals list**, and a **recent activity feed**.

---

### **Four Stat Cards** {#four-stat-cards}

**What they are:** Four small boxes at the top of the Dashboard, each showing one key number. These are the "vital signs" of the company at a glance.

| Card | What it shows |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Headcount** | Total number of employees currently at the company |
| **On Leave Today** | How many employees are on approved leave *today* |
| **Open Roles** | How many job positions are currently open/being hired for |
| **Next Payroll Date** | The date of the upcoming payroll run |

### **Headcount & Attrition Chart** {#headcount-&-attrition-chart}

**What it is:** A chart showing how the company's headcount has changed over the last 9 months. It tracks three things:

* **Joiners** — how many people were hired each month  
* **Leavers** — how many people left each month (resignations, terminations, etc.)  
* **Net** — the overall change (joiners minus leavers) for each month

### **Pending Approvals List** {#pending-approvals-list}

**What it is:** A list of items that are waiting on HR (or a relevant approver) to take action — things like leave requests, expense claims, new hire approvals, etc. Each item has Approve and Decline buttons right there in the list.

### **Recent Activity Feed** {#recent-activity-feed}

**What it is:** A running list/log of recent events happening across the company — things like new hires starting, employees going on leave, approvals that were processed, role changes, etc.

## **Recruitment — The Hiring Pipeline**

---

 {#recruitment-—-the-hiring-pipeline}

**What is the Recruitment tab?**

Recruitment is a **separate tab** from the core HR system, dedicated to hiring. It's kept apart from the main HR records because hiring is a different kind of workflow — it deals with *candidates* (people not yet employed), not *employees*. However, it's not fully isolated: once someone is hired, their information **flows into** the core HR system automatically, instead of living in two disconnected places.

This tab has two main parts: an **open requisitions table** and a **candidate kanban board**.

### **1\. Open Requisitions Table** {#1.-open-requisitions-table}

![][image1]

**What it is:** A table listing every open job position ("requisition") the company is currently hiring for. Each row shows:

* **Role** — the job title being hired for  
* **Department** — which team/department the role belongs to  
* **Hiring Manager** — who owns/is responsible for this hire  
* **Stage** — where this requisition currently stands in the hiring process (e.g., newly opened, actively interviewing, offer stage, closed, etc.)

### **2\. Kanban Board (Candidate Pipeline)** {#2.-kanban-board-(candidate-pipeline)}

![][image2]

**What it is:** A visual board that tracks candidates as they move through the hiring process, organized into columns representing each stage:

**Applied → Screening → Interview → Offer → Hired**

Each candidate is shown as a "card" that gets moved from column to column as they progress (or gets removed/rejected if they don't move forward).

**Clicking a candidate card:** Opens that candidate's **full profile**, which includes:

* **Resume**  
* **Source** — where the candidate came from (e.g., job board, referral, LinkedIn, etc.)  
* **Interview feedback** — notes/comments left by interviewers  
* **Scorecards** — structured ratings/evaluations from the interview process  
* **Stage history** — a timeline of which stages the candidate has moved through and when

### **3\. Key Automation: Hired → Draft Employee Record** {#3.-key-automation:-hired-→-draft-employee-record}

**What it does:** When a candidate's card is moved to the **"Hired"** stage, the system **automatically creates a draft employee record** in the core HR system. This draft is **pre-filled** using information already collected during the application process (e.g., name, contact info, role, department).

## **Employees — Employee Records**

---

 {#employees-—-employee-records}

### **Employee Directory (list view)** {#employee-directory-(list-view)}

* Table of all employees — Name, Department, Job Title, Status, Manager.  
* Search/filter by department, status, etc.  
* Clicking a row opens that employee's individual record.

### **Individual Employee Record — Sub-tabs:** {#individual-employee-record-—-sub-tabs:}

* **Personal** — contact info, address, emergency contacts, etc.  
* **Job** — title, department, manager, employment status, start date.  
* **Compensation** — current pay \+ full salary history.  
* **Documents** — the employee's digital **201 file** (contracts, IDs, certifications, clearances, and other downloadable records).

**Change Requests** *(new)*

* Table of all profile change requests submitted by this employee via the "Request Access" button on their Profile tab  
* Columns: Field(s) requested (e.g., Phone, Address, Bank Account), Old Value, New Value, Date Submitted, Status (Pending / Approved / Rejected)  
* HR can click a request to review details and any submitted documentation, then approve or reject  
* Approving here is what actually updates the employee's Personal/Job info — the employee-side Profile tab stays view-only until this happens

## **Time & Leave — HR's Leave Request Queue**

---

 {#time-&-leave-—-hr's-leave-request-queue}

### **Requests Table** {#requests-table}

* Lists all leave requests with approve/decline actions.  
* Requests land here automatically when employees submit them — no manual entry by HR.

**Key Automation**

* Approving a request instantly updates the employee's leave balance.

**Request Modal**

* Clicking a request opens a modal showing its full details (e.g., employee, leave type, dates, reason, balance, status).

## **Payroll — Runs the Pay Cycle**

---

 {#payroll-—-runs-the-pay-cycle}

*(Includes two sections within the same tab: Run Payroll and Payroll Inquiry)*

### **Run Payroll**

**"Run Payroll" Button**  
 Processes salaries, attendance, leave, and deductions together.  
 Outputs totals (gross / deductions / net).

**Per-Employee Payroll Table**  
 Displays a table of every employee showing their Name, Role, and Amount, each with an attached payslip and a "Mark as Done" button — so HR can see the full payroll list and how much each person is paid.

**Key Automation**  
 Once processing finishes, every employee's Payslips tab is automatically filled in — no manual computing.

### **Payroll Inquiry** {#payroll-inquiry}

**Request Inquiry Button**

* Employees submit pay-related inquiries through this button.

**Queue**

* HR manages inquiries through a Pending → In Progress → Done queue.  
* Follow-up with employees happens via Telegram.

## **Reimbursement — Expense Claims HR Manages**

---

 {#reimbursement-—-expense-claims-hr-manages}

### **Claims Table** {#claims-table}

* Lists all expense claims with actions: Approve / Reject / Mark Paid.  
* Claims arrive here automatically when an employee files one.  
* Approved claims roll into the next payroll run.

### **Claim Form Fields** {#claim-form-fields}

* **Category** — type of expense (e.g., Transportation & Travel, Food & Entertainment, Delivery & Logistics, Office Supplies, Online/Digital Purchases, Miscellaneous).  
* **Amount** — must be in PHP.  
* **Date** — date of the expense/receipt; claim must be filed within 15 calendar days (30 days if for business travel, with proof attached).  
* **Description** — business purpose of the expense (e.g., attendees \+ purpose for meals, intended use for supplies).  
* **Receipts** — valid proof of payment required (Official Receipt or approved digital proof); no receipt \= no reimbursement, no exceptions.

### **Employee-Facing View** {#employee-facing-view}

* **File a Claim** — form with Category (dropdown), Amount (₱), Date Incurred, Description, Receipt (file upload), and Submit Claim button.  
* **My Claims** — employee's own claim history with category, amount, description, date, and status (e.g., Approved).  
* HR is notified the moment a claim is submitted; the employee is notified when it's approved and paid.

## **Attendance**

---

 {#attendance}

### **Attendance Table** {#attendance-table}

* Log of employee time records — Time In, Time Out, hours rendered, status per day.

### **Attendance Alerts** {#attendance-alerts}

* Color-coded by severity: **Green / Yellow / Orange / Red**.  
* Applies to: Time In/Out issues, Tardiness, and Unauthorized Absence violations.

## [**Reports — Report Library**](?tab=t.6n0agqtyimp7)

---

 {#reports-—-report-library}

Library of six standard report types that can be built and exported.

### **Headcount & Movement** {#headcount-&-movement}

* Tracks joiners, leavers, and internal transfers over a chosen period.  
* Shows net headcount change by department and by month.  
* Filterable by department, location, and date range.

### **Attrition & Tenure** {#attrition-&-tenure}

* Splits attrition into voluntary and involuntary departures.  
* Flags regretted attrition (loss of high-value employees).  
* Plots tenure curves showing how long people stay before leaving.

### **Leave & Absence** {#leave-&-absence}

* Shows current leave balances by employee and by leave type.  
* Tracks utilization — how much allotted leave is actually taken.  
* Surfaces absence patterns (recurring days off, seasonal spikes).  
* Calculates liability accrual — financial obligation from unused leave.

### **Payroll & Cost** {#payroll-&-cost}

* Breaks down gross-to-net pay, including all deductions.  
* Calculates cost per head across teams or the whole organization.  
* Maintains run history for review/audit.

### **Recruitment Funnel** {#recruitment-funnel}

* Tracks time-to-hire from job posting to accepted offer.  
* Compares source effectiveness (referrals, job boards, agencies).  
* Reports offer acceptance rate.  
* Shown as a funnel: Applied → Screened → Interviewed → Offered → Hired.

### **Diversity & Pay Equity** {#diversity-&-pay-equity}

* Shows workforce representation across demographic categories.  
* Runs pay-gap analysis across groups doing similar work.  
* Tracks progression by cohort (promotion/pay growth over time).  
* Access typically restricted to HR and leadership.
